1.point: Open with the friends of God who are with God in secret and among people in the open, and say the chapter will follow the traveller the rest of the way back to people while still with God.
steps: Hook: the Munajat line and Imam Ali's words to Kumayl describe people who are both with God and at work among people
Those two halves (linked to the highest abode; calling people to God on earth) are what the chapter is about
Recall Chapter Twelve (sober return, annihilation a beginning) and state the chapter's claim: the road ends back among people and still with God; the Prophet and Imams walked it to the end

2.point: Annihilation closes only the first of four journeys; the second, travelled under God's guardianship, takes him through God's names and returns him to himself as a servant.
steps: There are four journeys, two to God and two back; the first ends in annihilation
The first journey is the book's road so far and is only a quarter of the way
The remaining journeys are made 'by God', i.e. under His wilaya, since the self is gone
The second journey examines what is reflected in the heart: God's names and attributes shown one by one, with a ceiling that only the Prophet is free of
It ends in baqa': the traveller returns to sobriety and knows himself a servant

3.point: The third journey turns the servant back to creation, seen as God's names at work, with certainty; the fourth keeps him among people, with God, able to guide them.
steps: The third journey turns back towards creation; he sees the three worlds as manifestations of God's names
What he sees gives certainty (the Ibrahim verse)
That certainty is for passing on: he can inform others and becomes the knower; Mutahhari: returns to guide people
The fourth journey, in creation by God, shows the reality of things and how everything returns to God, so he can guide people while united with God
Those who finished only the first journey find mixing with people hard; the fourth removes that difficulty, as in the Prophet

4.point: The complete return belongs first to the Prophet and the Imams, but the station is not exclusive, so the rest of us are called to walk towards it, staying in society, as far as God allows.
steps: The lectures give the third journey to a few high mystics and the fourth to the Prophet and then the Imams
Tabatabai describes the rank that holds both worlds and says it is perhaps exclusive to prophets, awliya and whoever God wishes
Tabatabai separates the office (exclusive) from the station of wilaya (not exclusive): the Prophet called his community to where he stood, citing the Ahzab verse
So both sources place the fullest return first in the Prophet and Imams and leave the road open
Following them asks of us, from the start, to stay in society while travelling

5.point: Imam al-Husayn shows the whole return in one life: as a beggar before God with his household around him at Arafah, and with and for his people at Karbala.
steps: Take one known life, as Khomeini points to Husayn's Arafah supplication; flag the reading as the book's own
The Arafah scene: surrounded by household, facing the Kaba, hands raised like a beggar, asking for fear of God as if seeing Him
Read the scene as both sides of the return at once
Karbala: he stayed with his people to the end; Khomeini links such prayer to service of others and to wielding the sword
Conclude: the completed journey came back to people while with God, and so to Karbala

¶1.label: advance
¶1.why: The hook: the Munajat line and Imam Ali's words to Kumayl introduce the people the chapter is about.

¶2.label: advance
¶2.why: Supplies why the two quotations sit together: both halves, linked to the highest abode and working among people. The Mutahhari sentence is a side link but the paragraph carries the step.

¶3.label: advance
¶3.why: Recalls Chapter Twelve in one sentence and states what the chapter will establish, including the Prophet, Imams and Husayn.

¶4.label: advance
¶4.why: Introduces the four journeys, their names and direction; annihilation is not the end.

¶5.label: advance
¶5.why: Places the book's road so far as the first journey and supplies the key step: it is only one quarter of the way. Veils and self-heart-spirit overlap the box but are needed here for the recap.

¶6.label: advance
¶6.why: Explains 'by God': once the self is gone the traveller is carried by wilaya, which the night-prayer line expresses.

¶7.label: advance
¶7.why: Defines the second journey as examining what is reflected in the heart. First sentence repeats ¶6's wilaya point and 'harder and more delightful' is asserted without use, but the step is new.

¶8.label: advance
¶8.why: The content of the second journey: taken through the names and attributes, with the ceiling that only the Prophet has no one above him, which ¶16 later uses.

¶9.label: advance
¶9.why: Ends the second journey in baqa' and servanthood and places Chapter Twelve's sober return on the map. Last sentence leans toward restate but the step is needed.

¶10.label: advance
¶10.why: The third journey: back towards creation, the three worlds seen as manifestations of the names, yielding certainty, with the Ibrahim verse introduced.

¶11.label: support
¶11.why: Glosses malakut and ties the verse's outcome (certainty) to the lectures' 'reassurance', which ¶12 picks up as 'certainty of this kind'.

¶12.label: advance
¶12.why: Certainty is for passing on: he can inform others, becomes the knower, and Mutahhari gives the same purpose, to guide people. The Bismillah example supports it in place.

¶13.label: advance
¶13.why: The fourth journey: what the Prophet is shown and that he lives among people while united with God to guide them.

¶14.label: support
¶14.why: Sets up the difficulty that ¶15 resolves: those who stopped after the first journey find mixing with people hard. The Tabatabai gnostic is a second illustration of the same point and could be trimmed.

¶15.label: advance
¶15.why: The fourth journey brings him down to the level of ordinary people, removing the difficulty ¶14 raised; for the Prophet mixing is easiest. Close to ¶13 but it supplies the resolution.

¶16.label: advance
¶16.why: Who walks it to the end: a few high mystics for the third, the Prophet and then the Imams for the fourth; uses ¶8's ceiling.

¶17.label: aside
¶17.why: That the Imams' inner knowledge stayed inside the Sharia is true and sourced but no later step uses it. Only the last sentence (Imams holding unity and plurality together) serves as a bridge to ¶18, and it could be folded into ¶18.

¶18.label: advance
¶18.why: Tabatabai names the rank that holds both worlds and says it is perhaps exclusive to prophets, awliya and whoever God wishes; the step the section turns on. The Mutahhari awliya sentence is a side link.

¶19.label: support
¶19.why: Describes the rank of ¶18 from inside and outside (states beyond the archangel; outwardly a human like you), filling out what the fullest return looks like. ¶21 would follow from ¶18 without it, so it is the weakest support.

¶20.label: aside
¶20.why: First sentence repeats the verse's meaning; the Sufyan al-Thawri story is a lesson in hidden zuhd that the argument about who completes the return does not use.

¶21.label: advance
¶21.why: Office exclusive, station not: the road is open and the Prophet's call implies the possibility, with the Ahzab verse cited.

¶22.label: support
¶22.why: First sentence unpacks the Ahzab verse that ¶21 cites. The second sentence ('Side by side, then...') restates the section's conclusion and could go.

¶23.label: advance
¶23.why: Supplies the 'rest of us' half: following the return asks staying in society from the start, which the lectures insist on against retreat.

¶24.label: advance
¶24.why: Chooses Husayn's life through Khomeini's pointer to the Arafah supplication and flags the section as the book's own reflection.

¶25.label: advance
¶25.why: The Arafah scene itself: household around him, facing the Kaba, begging posture, the request about his heart.

¶26.label: advance
¶26.why: The interpretive step: the scene holds both sides of the return at once. Short, and leans on ¶25, but it is the reading the section promised.

¶27.label: advance
¶27.why: Karbala: he stayed with his people to the last, and Khomeini ties such prayer to service of others and wielding the sword. The second sentence repeats ¶24's Khomeini claim.

¶28.label: restate
¶28.why: Summarises the chapter's conclusion already given in ¶3 and ¶22; the Mafatih sympathy line and the hand-off to the next chapter add no step.
